---
title: "Recessions"
---

The recessions that shaped when millennials entered the job market, faceted by the generation that was around 22, typical career-entry age, when each one started. Data cleaned in [table_sources.qmd](table_sources.qmd); this reads the result and plots it.

```{r}
#| label: fig-recessions
#| message: false
#| fig-cap: "GDP decline by US recession since 1945, faceted by generation at career-entry age"
#| fig-height: 7
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)

recessions <- read_csv("data/recessions_clean.csv") |>
  mutate(generation = factor(generation, levels = c(
    "Greatest Generation", "Silent Generation", "Baby Boomers",
    "Generation X", "Millennials", "Generation Z"
  )))

ggplot(recessions, 
  aes(
    x = fct_reorder(name, gdp_decline_pct), 
    y = gdp_decline_pct, fill = era)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  # facet_wrap(~ generation, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Dot-com bust" = "#d62728", "Financial crisis" = "#1f77b4",
    "COVID-19" = "#2ca02c", "Other" = "grey70"
  )) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, 
    y = "GDP decline, peak to trough (%)", 
    fill = "Era",
    title = "The recessions that shaped each generation's entry into the job market"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```
